issues.legal_issue: A deposit made under a general debtor-creditor procedure does not constitute payment or tender of rent that prevents eviction for rent default.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction for rent allegedly unpaid over an earlier period.
At the first hearing, the tenant tendered rent for only part of the claimed period, together with interest and costs.
The tenant relied on earlier deposits in court under a debtor-creditor statute as payment of the remaining rent; the deposits included amounts for future rent.
The rent statute provided for a tenant to avoid the consequence of default by tendering the arrears, interest, and costs at the first hearing, but provided no other procedure for depositing rent.
issues.conclusion: The deposits under the debtor-creditor statute did not cure the rent default or save the tenant from eviction; the eviction order was made.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 13(2)(i) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, a tenant in default may avoid eviction by making the prescribed tender at the first hearing. Section 31 of the East Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934, read in the context of that Act as a whole, concerns debtor-creditor payments and stopping interest, and does not provide a rent-deposit mechanism between landlords and tenants. Sections 19 and 6 of the rent statute, which restrict recovery of advance rent, further weigh against treating the debtor-creditor court as a rent-collection facility. The court rejected the contrary approach in Mam Chand v. Chhotu Ram and preferred the contrary single-judge decisions noted in that case.

rule.if: rent_eviction_proceeding and rent_due_not_timely_tendered and relied_on_general_debt_payment_deposit and rent_statute_limits_cure_to_prescribed_hearing_tender

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: A landlord seeks eviction of a tenant on the ground that rent was not paid or tendered.
predicates.rent_due_not_timely_tendered: Rent due for the relevant period was not paid or tendered within the required time.
predicates.relied_on_general_debt_payment_deposit: The tenant relies on a court deposit made under a general debtor-creditor payment procedure as payment or tender of rent.
predicates.rent_statute_limits_cure_to_prescribed_h: The rent procedure provides a specified hearing-stage tender as the means to cure the default and does not authorize the relied-on alternative deposit as a rent tender.

issues.definition: When a rent-eviction proceeding involves untimely rent payment and the tenant relies on a general debt-payment deposit rather than the rent procedure's prescribed hearing-stage tender, the rent default remains uncured.

issues.legal_issue: An allegation of inaccurate statements in an application for special leave does not justify rejecting the application when the statements are not shown to be deliberate falsehoods and the issue described was the issue considered below.
material_facts: The respondent objected to special leave, alleging that the appellant had made inaccurate and misleading statements about whether the validity of the deposits had been raised before the Rent Controller and the appellate authority.
The High Court stated that the validity of the deposits was the only point considered by the courts below.
The court found no basis to regard the appellant's statements as deliberate falsehoods of the kind involved in the cited cases.
issues.conclusion: The objection to the grant of special leave was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Hari Narain v. Badri Das and Rajabhai Abdul Rehman Munshi v. Vasudev Dhanjibhai Mody concerned gross misstatements in which an applicant had deliberately made false statements or pleas. The court distinguished those cases because the alleged inaccuracies here did not establish deliberate falsehood, and the deposit issue had been considered below.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and material_inaccuracy_alleged and issue_was_considered_below and not deliberate_false_statement_established

predicates.special_leave_appeal: A party seeks special leave to appeal from a lower-court decision.
predicates.material_inaccuracy_alleged: The opposing party alleges that the applicant misstated material facts about the proceedings below.
predicates.issue_was_considered_below: The lower courts considered the issue to which the alleged inaccuracy relates.
predicates.deliberate_false_statement_established: The record establishes that the applicant deliberately made a false statement or plea.

issues.definition: When a special-leave appeal is opposed on an alleged material inaccuracy, the issue was considered below, and deliberate falsehood is not established, the objection is rejected.
